question: Should I Refund Through WooCommerce or the Gateway Dashboard?
metaDescription: Through WooCommerce, whenever possible — it keeps order status, stock, and reporting in sync automatically instead of drifting out of step.
shortAnswer: Through WooCommerce, whenever the gateway integration supports it. Refunding from the order screen in WooCommerce automatically calls the gateway's API to reverse the actual charge, then updates the order's status, records the refund amount, and (if configured) restocks the items — all in one action. Refunding directly in the gateway's own dashboard reverses the charge but leaves WooCommerce completely unaware, which drifts the order status and reporting out of sync with what actually happened.

bodyHtml:
Why the Order Matters

WooCommerce's built-in refund action on an order calls the connected gateway's refund API directly, so the money genuinely returns to the customer exactly as it would from the gateway's own dashboard — the difference is that WooCommerce also records the refund against the order, adjusts reporting totals, and can automatically restock items if that setting is enabled. A refund issued only in the gateway's dashboard skips all of that; the money moves, but WooCommerce has no idea it happened unless told separately.

When Gateway-Direct Refunds Happen Anyway

  • The gateway integration doesn't support API refunds for a specific payment method (some offline or less common gateways only support refunding manually), leaving no choice but to refund directly and then update the WooCommerce order by hand.
  • A partial refund scenario the WooCommerce order UI doesn't cleanly support, occasionally pushing an admin toward the gateway dashboard instead, though most modern integrations do handle partial refunds correctly.
  • An order that's already been deleted or is otherwise inaccessible in WooCommerce, where the gateway dashboard is the only remaining way to process a refund at all.

Keeping Things in Sync

  1. Always try the WooCommerce order refund action first, confirming it successfully calls the gateway before assuming a manual gateway-side refund is needed.
  2. If a gateway-direct refund is unavoidable, manually add an order note and adjust the order status in WooCommerce afterward so reporting stays accurate.
  3. Periodically reconcile gateway transaction records against WooCommerce order data if manual gateway-side refunds happen with any regularity, to catch any drift early.

Dealing with refund/reporting mismatches after some manual gateway refunds? See WooCommerce fixes.
